Course · Italian for English speakers

Learn Italian with the grammar explained.

A complete course in the standard Italian of Italy for English speakers, from pronunciation and first words to the passato remoto, register and regional Italian at C1. Each module explains its grammar directly, then practises it with exercises whose feedback says what was wrong and why.

Start learning free

The whole course, the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test are free. CILS, CELI and PLIDA practice papers, specializations, stories, conversation practice and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

The course: 8 tiers, 76 modules

  1. Tier 1 · A1 · Sounds and first wordsPronunciation and spelling, greetings, nouns and articles, essere, numbers.
  2. Tier 2 · A1 · Everyday basicsThe present of -are, -ere and -ire verbs, avere, adjectives, questions.
  3. Tier 3 · A1–A2 · Daily lifeIrregular, modal and reflexive verbs, articulated prepositions, the partitive.
  4. Tier 4 · A2 · The pastThe passato prossimo and the imperfect, object pronouns.
  5. Tier 5 · A2–B1 · Building fluencyCi and ne, combined pronouns, future, conditional, imperative.
  6. Tier 6 · B1 · IntermediateThe present subjunctive, the trapassato, reported speech.
  7. Tier 7 · B2 · Upper intermediateThe imperfect subjunctive, if-clauses, the passive and si.
  8. Tier 8 · C1 · AdvancedThe passato remoto, style, idioms, spoken and regional Italian.

All eight tiers are free.

How it teaches

A course that explains, then checks

  • 1

    Grammar taught directly

    Articles and articulated prepositions, essere or avere in the passato prossimo, ci and ne and the subjunctive each get their own modules, explained in plain English before you practise them.

  • 2

    Feedback that says why

    Every answer gets feedback with the reason and a link to the grammar rule, and the exercises you got wrong come back at the end.

  • 3

    Every Italian word can be tapped

    Tap any word in a lesson, exercise or text for its meaning, its forms and audio, and add it to your vocabulary.

  • 4

    The Italian of Italy, and its regions

    The standard Italian of Italy, with modules on spoken Italian and on Italian across Italy and beyond in the last tier.

  • 5

    Speaking with pronunciation feedback

    Speaking exercises check your pronunciation of Italian sentences, word by word.

  • 6

    Common traps

    Short units on the mistakes English speakers make in Italian, from false friends and articles where English has none to one English verb that needs two Italian ones.

Exam preparation

Practice papers for CILS, CELI and PLIDA

The course has two timed practice papers for each level of three Italian certificates, in their task formats with original content: CILS from the Università per Stranieri di Siena (A1 to C2), CELI from the Università per Stranieri di Perugia (CELI Impatto to CELI 5) and PLIDA from the Società Dante Alighieri (A1 to C2). That is 18 exams and 36 papers. They are part of Premium.

  • CILS, CELI and PLIDA practice papers: what the B1 exams ask, what the papers cover and where they differ from the real exams.

Questions

Common questions

Is the Italian course really free?
Yes. All 76 modules from A1 to C1, the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test are free, with no limit on lessons. Premium adds the extras listed above.
Which Italian does Glossa teach?
The standard Italian of Italy, with a module on spoken Italian and one on Italian across Italy and beyond.
I already know some Italian. Do I have to start from the beginning?
No. The placement test finds the tier to start from.
How far does the course go?
To C1: the last tier covers the passato remoto, implicit clauses, the fine points of the subjunctive, register and style, idioms and proverbs, spoken and regional Italian, history, literature and law.
Can it prepare me for an Italian certificate such as PLIDA B1 for citizenship?
The course covers the grammar and vocabulary from A1 to C1, and Premium adds timed practice papers for every level of CILS, CELI and PLIDA, including the B1 exams. The papers have no speaking test and give no grade, so they are practice, not a prediction of your result. Which certificate an application needs is decided by the Italian authorities that handle it.
